Probe status is provenance, not evidence, and non-dispositive by construction; it neither establishes nor is required to establish the underlying category disposition, which is independently excluded on affirmative full-text grounds.

basis: Full text (Congress.gov accepted page and the sole GovInfo 'is' version) contains a single operative section limiting expenditure of Public Law 119-21 funds on ICE/CBP hiring. No CDFI Fund, community development financial institution, Treasury CDFI program, or related award/certification provision appears in the title, text, or actions. Official CRS summary is authoritatively unavailable; that absence is treated as neutral and no inference is drawn from it.

The measure's entire operative content is an appropriations restriction on immigration enforcement personnel costs. Nothing in the title 'ICE Funding Accountability Act', the full text, or the referral to Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs touches the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, its funding structure, leadership, rulemaking, UDAAP authority, or supervisory jurisdiction. Summary unavailability is neutral.

No provision addresses federal credit union charters, board governance, bylaws, officials' compensation, conversions, mergers, or the Federal Credit Union Act. The two-section bill addresses only salaries, recruitment, advertising, and bonuses for ICE and CBP agents or officers funded under Public Law 119-21. Absence of charter/governance content is recorded as neutral, not as negative evidence.

The full text imposes no requirements on credit card issuers, late fees, overdraft or NSF fees, APR caps, or consumer fee disclosures. The only monetary terms present are 'salaries', 'retention or sign on bonuses' payable to federal immigration enforcement personnel, which are federal employment compensation items, not consumer financial product fees. Neutral absence.

No comparative treatment of credit unions versus banks, acquisition of bank assets by credit unions, parity provisions, or competitive-advantage findings appear anywhere in the reviewed record. The measure is confined to a spending limitation on ICE/CBP hiring. Neutral absence; this is also a non-scoring slot.

Nothing addresses net worth ratios, risk-based capital, prompt corrective action, supplemental or secondary capital, or subordinated debt. The reviewed text contains only the ICE/CBP personnel funding prohibition. Neutral absence.

Affirmative textual hook exists and is fully accounted for: the long title and Section 2 expressly reference 'the One Big Beautiful Bill Act' and 'Public Law 119-21'. That reference is the sole cause of the category match, and it is an alias-string collision rather than substantive overlap. The operative provision does not amend the Internal Revenue Code, does not touch section 501(c)(1) or 501(c)(14) exemption, unrelated business income tax, or any credit union revenue treatment; it prohibits spending already-appropriated Public Law 119-21 funds on salaries, recruitment, advertising, and retention or sign-on bonuses for ICE and CBP agents or officers hired on or after enactment. Referral to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs rather than the Committee on Finance corroborates the non-revenue character. Finding is grounded in affirmative content, not in the absence of credit union terms.

No data protection, breach notification, Gramm-Leach-Bliley safeguards, information sharing, or cybersecurity provision appears in the title, either reviewed text version, or the action record. The measure is a personnel-funding restriction only. Neutral absence.

Although the bill concerns federal law enforcement personnel at ICE and CBP, it contains no provision on military installations, on-base financial services, Military Lending Act protections, servicemember or defense credit union operations, or DoD banking arrangements. Immigration enforcement staffing is not a defense credit union matter. Neutral absence.

No examination cycle, exam appeals, ombudsman, supervisory guidance, or prudential regulator oversight provision is present. The word 'accountability' appears only in the short title 'ICE Funding Accountability Act' and refers to federal appropriations oversight, not financial institution supervision. Neutral absence.

Nothing addresses common bond, community charter boundaries, underserved area expansion, associational groups, or NCUA field of membership rules. The reviewed record covers only the ICE/CBP hiring expenditure prohibition. Neutral absence.

No provision addresses payment fraud, elder financial exploitation, scam reimbursement, check or wire fraud, or fraud reporting obligations. The measure restricts use of appropriated funds for immigration enforcement staffing and creates no anti-fraud duty. Neutral absence.
No reference to interchange fees, the Durbin Amendment, routing mandates, network exclusivity, or debit/credit card acceptance appears in any reviewed version. Neutral absence.

No member business lending cap, commercial lending authority, SBA participation, or agricultural lending provision is present. The bill's only subject is the Public Law 119-21 funding restriction for ICE and CBP hiring. Neutral absence.
No mortgage origination, servicing, TRID/HMDA, appraisal, GSE, FHA, or housing affordability provision appears in the title, full text, or actions. Neutral absence.

The measure is a spending limitation, but it applies exclusively to amounts appropriated or otherwise made available under Public Law 119-21 for ICE and CBP personnel. It does not address the NCUA operating budget, overhead transfer rate, the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund, normal operating level, or premiums/distributions. The appropriations subject matter does not create an NCUA nexus. Neutral absence.

No provision concerns payment systems, ACH, real-time or instant payments, FedNow, wire transfers, stablecoins, or settlement. References to paying salaries and bonuses are federal compensation mechanics, not payments-system policy. Neutral absence.
No artificial intelligence, digital assets, cloud/core processing, open banking, or fintech partnership provision appears in any reviewed version. Neutral absence.

No TCPA, autodialer, prior express consent, robocall, revocation-of-consent, or FCC communications provision is present. The term 'advertise for hiring' in Section 2(2) concerns federal recruitment advertising and has no telephony or consumer-contact regulatory dimension. Neutral absence.

matched_category_basis: Matched on the reconciliation-vehicle alias 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' / 'Public Law 119-21' appearing in the long title and Section 2. That vehicle is associated with credit union tax status debate, but here it is referenced only as the source of appropriations being restricted for ICE/CBP hiring; no credit union tax provision is enacted, amended, or referenced. Search membership treated as provenance only, never as decision evidence.
reason: S.3933 is the 'ICE Funding Accountability Act', a two-section measure whose sole operative provision bars amounts appropriated or otherwise made available under Public Law 119-21 from being expended to pay salaries of, or to recruit, advertise for hiring, or pay retention or sign-on bonuses to, ICE and CBP agents or officers hired on or after enactment. The category match is fully explained by the literal phrase 'the One Big Beautiful Bill Act' in the long title and 'Public Law 119-21' in Section 2. The bill does not amend the Internal Revenue Code, does not address the federal income tax exemption of credit unions, unrelated business income tax, or any revenue treatment of financial cooperatives; it restricts downstream spending of funds that statute already provided. Referral to Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs rather than Finance corroborates the non-revenue character, and the sponsor role and both IntroReferral actions are consistent with an immigration-enforcement appropriations measure. All expected text versions (one, the GovInfo 'is' version, locally parsed and content-verified) were reviewed and confirm the Congress.gov page. Exclusion rests on affirmative operative content, not on the non-appearance of credit union terminology.

matched_category_basis: Pure title/full-text alias match on 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act'. Probe is flagged membership_non_dispositive and non-scoring; alias presence is affirmatively documented and affirmatively explained as a funding-source citation rather than a credit union tax provision.
reason: This T4 probe is expressly non-dispositive and is designed to surface measures whose titles or texts invoke the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' alias. The probe fired correctly at the string level: the long title and Section 2 of S.3933 both reference that Act and Public Law 119-21. However, the referenced Act appears purely as the appropriations source being constrained, and the measure's substance is an immigration-enforcement personnel spending limitation with no credit union, tax, or financial-institution content in any of the one expected and reviewed text versions. The probe therefore confirms alias provenance but supplies no material nexus to the underlying scoring category, and it cannot independently support inclusion.
